item.title: The Ride Platform Expands Wheelbase as Insurance Distribution Channel
item.description: (Image source: The Ride Platform homepage.) The Ride Platform (Austin and London) has launched Wheelbase 2.0, expanding its fleet-management platform with AI agents and an App Exchange that creates a broader distribution channel for insurance and other services used by independent mobility operators. Aaron Ammar, Chief Insurance Officer, The Ride Platform, says Wheelbase gives carrier and reinsurance partners visibility into bookings, digital check-ins, renter verification, telematics and fleet maintenance within a single system. Opening a Broader Insurance Distribution Channel The Wheelbase App Exchange launches with Roamly Insurance & Protection for embedded coverage and Roamly Fleet for telematics, along with third-party applications for bookkeeping, toll management and vehicle tracking.

item.title: GreenieRE Selects INTX Re for Reinsurance Data Management
item.description: “We selected INTX Re to build more consistency into how we manage bordereaux as our business grows.” GreenieRE focuses on reinsurance solutions supporting clean-energy technologies and projects, including risks for which data formats may vary and historical loss information may be limited. (Image source: GreenieRE homepage.) GreenieRE (Boston) has selected INTX Insurance Software (Austin, Texas) to strengthen management of premium, exposure and loss reporting across its growing network of insurance and program partners. The impact-focused reinsurer is initially using the bordereaux management capabilities of INTX Re, INTX’s platform for assumed reinsurance.

item.title: Penn River Launches TotalityOne to Simplify Life and Annuity Technology
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) Penn River (Newtown Square, Pa.) has launched TotalityOne , a modular new business and policy administration offering designed to give life and annuity carriers access to multiple technology and service providers while placing responsibility for integration and vendor coordination with Penn River. TotalityOne is designed to shift that responsibility to Penn River, combining its policy administration core with Solvrays’ orchestration technology and other vendors’ components under one contract. Powered by workflow orchestration technology from Solvrays (Charlotte, N.C.), the offering combines Penn River’s cloud-native policy administration core with components supporting illustrations, commissions, portals, underwriting, claims and outsourced operations.

item.title: The New Corporate Status Symbol Is How Much AI Access You Have
item.description: Companies are quietly sorting workers into different tiers of access as they determine which roles deserve more spend. Other companies are being more selective, giving some teams, such as engineering, unfettered access to the best models and letting other workers get by with more basic options. As employers make those calculations, the differences in access are contributing to a new kind of workplace hierarchy, according to executives and consultants.

item.title: Texas Agencies Partner in Safety Campaign to End Traffic Deaths
item.description: “Each life lost is a reminder of why we all need to work together to end this streak of daily deaths.” Beginning this week, Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) troopers will distribute safe driving tips during traffic stops for two weeks. We are proud to partner with TxDOT to remind drivers that getting home safely is a responsibility we all share, and together we can end the streak.” In 2025, Texas recorded 3,763 traffic deaths, down nearly 10% from 4,162 in 2024. 7, 2000, more than 95,000 people have been killed in traffic crashes on Texas roads.

item.title: Man sentenced over £154m fake takeover bid targeting UK-listed company
item.description: Christopher Woolcott has today been given a 2-year prison sentence, suspended for 2 years, after staging a £154m fake takeover bid for Touchstone Exploration Inc. Mr Woolcott built a sizeable stake in Touchstone, an oil and gas listed company. Therese Chambers, executive director of enforcement and market oversight at the FCA, said: 'Mr Woolcott's fake takeover bid was a calculated attempt to profit by manipulating the market.

item.title: Anthropic Seeks Record $88.5B Tied To Public Market Debut
item.description: Anthropic is seeking to secure up to $88.5 billion in its planned IPO and a concurrent private placement, potentially making it the largest-ever fundraise tied to a public market debut. Put together, it’s a record-setting capital haul for a company making its market debut, which Anthropic is expected to do later this month on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT. That said, even at $1.4 trillion, Anthropic would still be going public at the second-highest valuation in history, topped only by SpaceX ’s June debut.

item.title: Our ability to invest consistently (in ILS) is a huge advantage: Quantedge CEO
item.description: Quantedge Capital, the Singapore-based hedge fund asset manager, recognises that consistency in terms of its capital deployment to the insurance-linked securities asset class is key, as it enables the firm to be there when losses hit and it can benefit from hardening prices, CEO Suhaimi Zainul-Abidin explained in a recent podcast interview. Speaking with the Top Traders Unplugged podcast, Zainul-Abidin explained that how Quantedge Capital thinks about risk premia across all the asset classes it allocates to, which is helpful in understanding how the firm thinks about the ILS asset class and reinsurance. Quantedge manages approaching US $8 billion in its flagship systematic global hedge fund strategy, which has allocations across multiple asset classes such as equities, bonds, commodities, currencies and insurance-linked securities and had delivered a 20.9% net annualised return as of September 30th 2026.

item.title: Constantly evolving reinsurance market creates opportunities: Lockton Re’s Bisset
item.description: Robert Bisset, CEO, North America at global reinsurance broker Lockton Re, described the current reinsurance market as healthy and constantly evolving, with some divergence in appetite across certain lines of business creating opportunities. In an interview with Reinsurance News, Bisset emphasised that the global reinsurance market is healthy, with plentiful capital, robust competition and options available for clients. “Our job at Lockton Re is to understand where the market is moving in order to bring the best solutions and capabilities together to ensure we are creating the optimal outcomes for our clients.” Bisset said reinsurer discipline is broadly holding as market conditions soften, although current supply-and-demand dynamics are tipping the scales further in favour of buyers.

item.title: MS Transverse names Grippa as new Chief Commercial Officer
item.description: MS Transverse, a specialty insurance platform that works with programme administrators and managing general agents (MGAs), has announced the appointment of Anthony Grippa as Chief Commercial Officer (CCO). He is joining the company from BMS Re, where he most recently served as Chief Strategy Officer, and was a member of the U.S. He will be a strong addition to our leadership team and I am pleased to welcome him.” “MS Transverse has established a distinctive position as the leading hybrid fronting carrier for programs and MGAs, backed by the strength of MS&AD,” said Grippa.

item.title: Radian reports 106% revenue increase for Q3’26 as net premiums rise following Inigo deal
item.description: Radian Group Inc., a US financial services company operating in mortgage and specialty insurance, has reported a total revenue hike of 106% to $624 million for the third quarter of 2026, as net premiums earned rose to $548 million, of which 57%, or $311 million, came from the specialty segment following the firm’s acquisition of Inigo. Total revenue more than doubled year-over-year with the addition of Inigo, and the strategic rationale for the acquisition is already showing up in our results. For the quarter, Radian reported a net income from continuing operations of $172 million, compared to $153 million in Q3’25.

item.title: SpaceX Plans $24 Billion Data Center and Gas Plant in Texas
item.description: SpaceX plans to construct, own and operate a gas-fired power plant and super-compute facility at its company town in Starbase, Texas, according to a notice of a public hearing on the city’s website. The proposal is the latest sign that CEO Elon Musk is seeking to vertically integrate SpaceX’s value chain for natural gas, the primary power-plant fuel that data center developers are using to get the facilities up and running. SpaceX also plans to build its own gas-fired power plant to support the massive semiconductor manufacturing facility it’s developing in Grimes County, outside of Houston, with Tesla Inc.

item.title: AM Best Revises Outlook to Stable for Members of Texas Farm Bureau Insurance Group
item.description: AM Best has revised the outlook to stable from negative for the Long-Term Issuer Credit Ratings (Long-Term ICRs) and affirmed the Financial Strength Rating (FSR) of B++ (Good) and the Long-Term ICRs of “bbb+” (Good) for the members of Texas Farm Bureau Insurance Group. The ratings reflect Texas Farm Bureau Insurance Group’s balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as strong, as well as its marginal operating performance, neutral business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management (ERM). The revision of the outlook to stable from negative for the Long-Term ICRs reflects improvement in the group’s recent operating performance metrics driven by management’s various initiatives including rate increases and underwriting refinement, as well as more benign weather.

item.title: Indiana AG: Rental Home Operator to Pay $48M Settlement
item.description: Indiana Attorney General Todd Rokita on Tuesday announced a settlement with Progress Residential, LLC and Pretium Partners, LLC, one of the nation’s largest owners and operators of single-family rental homes, resolving allegations that the companies engaged in deceptive and unfair practices affecting renters, including Indiana residents. Under the settlement, the companies must make significant changes to their business practices that will benefit tenants in Indiana and across the country. The settlement provides $48.5 million in monetary relief for consumers nationwide and requires sweeping reforms to the companies’ business practices.

item.title: Optio Group acquires Norwegian specialty MGA SAFE Forsikring
item.description: Optio Group, the independent specialty MGA, has acquired Norwegian specialty MGA SAFE Forsikring (SAFE) for an undisclosed sum. SAFE joins Optio's Norwegian platform alongside S Insurance and AGS Forsikring. "We are delighted to welcome SAFE Forsikring to Optio.

item.title: The Flaw in 'Human-in-the-Loop'
item.description: The notion that there must always be a "human in the loop" has become de rigueur in any discussion of AI implementation in business. Now, an article in Harvard Business Review offers a similar view about the dangers of having a "human in the loop" to supervise work done by AIs. Each exception a person handles teaches the system to handle that exception; the better the data, the smaller the scope of human validation needed in the future." The article says the lack of reliability of the humans in the loop is actually just the start of the problem.

item.title: Jewelers Mutual acquires IFS Inforsure
item.description: Jewelers Mutual acquired IFS Inforsure, a Pasadena, California-based provider of insured shipping solutions for jewelry, watches and other high-value items. The acquisition expands Jewelers Mutual’s protected shipping capabilities and its broader offering of insurance and business services for the jewelry industry. IFS founder Jeroen Sparreboom said joining Jewelers Mutual would allow the company to accelerate the development of new solutions for the jewelry and watch industries.

item.title: RiverStone assumes $400 million SiriusPoint legacy portfolio
item.description: RiverStone International has completed a loss portfolio transfer with SiriusPoint, assuming a portfolio of legacy reinsurance liabilities with net liabilities of approximately $400 million. SiriusPoint CEO Scott Egan said the deal further simplifies the company’s business, strengthens its capital position and closes the chapter on its legacy portfolio. The transaction is RiverStone’s first with SiriusPoint.

item.title: THREE refreshes brand, emphasizes agent distribution
item.description: THREE by Berkshire Hathaway has launched a new website and refreshed brand as it emphasizes its position as an admitted commercial insurer built for agents. In a November 10 update, President Brandon Bauer said the company’s development had outpaced its communication, leaving a perception that THREE was primarily a direct-to-consumer business with a narrow specialty or E&S appetite. THREE combines business liability, property, cyber, commercial auto and workers’ compensation in one policy, with one submission and payment.

item.title: Allstate’s AI Ecosystem to Include a Personal Agentic Assistant for Customers
item.description: The next stop in Allstate’s journey with artificial intelligence – a personal agentic assistant for consumers. CEO Tom Wilson revealed that customers could expect an Allstate PAA early in 2027. “If they don’t feel like calling an Allstate agent – or feel like getting on our website – and they just want to have a PAA do that, we’re fine with that.” Wilson said personal lines new business is up 125% over 2019, and currently split about eventually between exclusive agents, independent agents, and direct-to-consumer.

item.title: Startup Founders Are Using AI To File Patents. Here’s Where DIY Becomes A Liability.
item.description: It’s how much founders can safely do themselves and when legal expertise becomes essential. Founders can use AI to organize technical documentation, summarize existing patents and identify potentially relevant prior art. Patents can help startups establish competitive advantage, attract investors and protect innovations.

item.title: The Crunchbase Unicorn Board Tops 1,900 Companies In October, With 34 Companies Joining — Half Under 4 Years Old
item.description: Last month’s new unicorn cohort also highlighted how quickly this AI cycle is awarding some companies with billion-dollar-plus valuations: Half of October’s new unicorns are less than 4 years old, and nine companies that joined the board during the month did so via seed or Series A raises. A total of 34 companies joined The Crunchbase Unicorn Board in October, adding more than $96 billion in value and $14.8 billion in total funding to the board. The Crunchbase Unicorn Board is a curated list that includes private unicorn companies with post-money valuations of $1 billion or more and is based on Crunchbase data.

item.title: ILS expansion beyond cat must be driven by pricing, structure, understanding: Doris, Twelve Securis
item.description: While the ILS market has moved beyond traditional property catastrophe risk and expanded into emerging perils such as cyber, casualty and specialty lines in recent years, Cahal Doris of Twelve Securis has expressed that this growth must be driven by pricing, structure and understanding, and not simply for the sake of expanding the market. Speaking to Artemis around the reinsurance conference season, Doris, who serves as Chief Investment Officer ILS at the firm, outlined that Twelve Securis views the current ILS market as being very healthy. “We remain positive about innovation beyond natural catastrophe risk, but expansion should not happen simply for the sake of expanding the ILS universe,” Doris stressed.

item.title: VIG Re lifts target to €60m for debut Charles Bridge Re catastrophe bond
item.description: VIG Re, the reinsurance arm of Vienna Insurance Group, is now aiming to slightly upsize its debut catastrophe bond sponsorship, raising the target to secure a larger €60 million of fully-collateralized European windstorm retrocession from the Charles Bridge Re 2026 DAC issuance, Artemis has learned. VIG Re made its debut in the catastrophe bond market for the first time last month. Initially the company was seeking €50 million of retrocessional reinsurance windstorm protection from investors with this debut Charles Bridge Re deal.

item.title: Munich Re teams with Wawanesa & WWF-Canada to launch parametric river flood solution
item.description: Reinsurance firm Munich Re has partnered with Wawanesa and World Wildlife Fund Canada (WWF-Canada), to develop and launch a parametric river flood insurance solution that will deliver rapid funding to safeguard nature-based restoration across the Wolastoq (Saint John River) watershed. Under the parametric structure, Wawanesa funding will be triggered by independently measured river levels, and if predetermined river conditions are met, Wawanesa will provide up to $1 million in funding each year, capped at a maximum of $3 million over a three-year period, to WWF-Canada. The parametric arrangement was developed with support from Munich Re Canada, alongside climate-peril expertise from reinsurance broker Marsh Re.

item.title: Gallagher appoints Rawden Leigh as Head of Retail in its Financial Institutions practice
item.description: Gallagher, a global insurance broking and risk management company, has announced the appointment of Rawden Leigh as Head of Retail in its Financial Institutions practice. Based in London, Leigh will lead Gallagher’s client proposition for retail financial institutions across the UK and Europe. Rawden brings impressive knowledge of the risks facing financial institutions and he is a fantastic asset to our growing team.” Leigh added, “Gallagher has a strong reputation across the financial institutions market and is a business with real momentum and an entrepreneurial culture.

item.title: Insurance market must become more ‘risk aware and not risk off,’ says Lloyd’s Turk
item.description: The primary challenge facing the insurance market is the deeply interconnected nature of today’s geopolitical and technological landscape, Rachel Turk, Lloyd’s Chief of Performance & Strategy, highlighted during AM Best’s recent Europe Insurance Market Briefing in London. Because of this, she argues that modern underwriters must become “geopolitically aware” to anticipate trade impacts, market shocks, and strict liability issues. The executive urges the market to be more “risk aware and not risk off,” with the fundamental mindset that the “objective should be to find a way to say yes to insuring this, rather than finding reasons to say no.” “The only way you can do that is to genuinely understand the environment in which we are operating, even when it’s becoming a bit more complicated,” she added.

item.title: Goosehead estimates Q3’26 revenue growth of 17%
item.description: Goosehead attributed core revenue growth to continued improvement in client retention and strong new business generation, driven by growth in total producers and improved franchise productivity. These capabilities are strengthening client relationships, expanding the ways we reach and serve clients, and positioning Goosehead to capture the substantial growth opportunity ahead.” For the full year 2026, Goosehead reaffirmed its guidance, expecting organic total revenue growth of between 12% and 19%. Goosehead Insurance, Inc., an independent personal lines insurance agency, has estimated total revenues of between $108.8 million and $110.8 million, an increase of approximately 17% at the mid-point of the range compared to an estimated $92.9 million to $94.9 million in the same period a year earlier.

item.title: Nvidia, CEO Huang Sued Over Disclosures Related to Suspected Chinese Spy
item.description: Nvidia and Chief Executive Jensen Huang were sued on Oct. 9 in a proposed class action accusing them of defrauding shareholders by concealing Huang’s ties with a suspected Chinese spy. According to a complaint filed in federal court in San Jose, California, the defendants misled shareholders about Huang’s alleged affair with Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed who is not related to him, and did not disclose that the matter raised national security concerns that threatened Nvidia’s reputation and business prospects.

item.title: Workers’ Compensation Claims Triggered Probes of Walmart for Child Labor Violations
item.description: Pennsylvania announced a $7.8 million settlement with Walmart for violations of the state’s Child Labor Act in what the Shapiro Administration said is the largest child labor enforcement action in Pennsylvania history. Investigations were triggered by reports of workers’ compensation claims related to minors. The Bureau of Labor Law Compliance (BLLC) began investigating Walmart in February 2025 after receiving referrals from the Bureau of Workers’ Compensation about minors who were injured while working at Walmart stores.

item.title: Nvidia-Backed Fireworks AI Notifies Customers of Its Second Hack in Weeks
item.description: Fireworks AI, a popular startup that helps companies run artificial intelligence models, notified customers on Monday of a security breach in which their data was accessed, its second known hack in a matter of weeks. A Fireworks spokesperson said the company is “actively working with our customers to manage the incident, including Notion, Cursor and others.” Fireworks has over 10,000 customers, including the legal tech firm Harvey, productivity software startup Notion and coding company Cursor, according to its website. At the time, the startup said it was investigating the matter and working with a cybersecurity firm “to assist with the incident.” On Monday, Fireworks AI confirmed in the post that its investigation of the early October breach uncovered impacts to customers’ account and billing information.

item.title: InsurGrid launches AI-powered Policy Change Monitoring for P&C agencies
item.description: InsurGrid, the policy data collection and AI workflow platform for property and casualty (P&C) insurance agencies, has launched Policy Change Monitoring, a service that refreshes declaration pages and policy data for connected clients every 15 days and alerts agencies when a policy is cancelled, reinstated, renewed, not renewed, or materially changed. Policy Change Monitoring keeps checking connected policies in the background and tells the right person what changed, field by field, so they can call the client first and decide what to do next," said Rohit Mittal, CEO of InsurGrid. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in San Francisco, InsurGrid turns declaration pages and carrier documents into structured, quote-ready policy data for intake, policy comparison, renewal, ACORD and COI, proposal, and rating workflows.

item.title: QBE Australia Pacific appoints Nigel Hawtin as Chief Transformation & Operations Officer
item.description: The post QBE Australia Pacific appoints Nigel Hawtin as Chief Transformation & Operations Officer appeared first on Insurtech Insights . QBE Insurance has appointed Nigel Hawtin as Chief Transformation & Operations Officer for its Australia Pacific business, effective 10 December 2026, subject to regulatory approval. He has a deep understanding of our business and how operations and transformation connect, and I’m delighted to welcome him to our Executive Management Board," said Jonathan Groves, CEO of QBE Australia Pacific.

item.title: KRW 2.26tn deal for Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance to take control of Canopius
item.description: The post KRW 2.26tn deal for Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance to take control of Canopius appeared first on Insurtech Insights . Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance (SFMI) has agreed to acquire an additional 40.6% stake in Lloyd's specialty (re)insurer Canopius, taking its ownership to 80.6%. Building on seven years of trust between Canopius and SFMI, we will combine our strengths to solidify our position in the Lloyd’s market and pursue further global expansion, including in the US," said Munhwa (Marvin) Lee, Chief Executive Officer & President of Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance.

item.title: Tune Protect expands Airpaz partnership to three more markets
item.description: Tune Protect has expanded its partnership with online travel booking platform Airpaz to offer embedded travel insurance in Indonesia, Thailand and the Philippines, following its Malaysia launch in 2025. The partnership, managed through reinsurance arm Tune Protect Re, allows customers to purchase travel insurance during flight bookings on Airpaz’s website and mobile app. Tune Protect Re CEO Janet Chin said the company also sees opportunities to extend the Airpaz collaboration into other regional markets.

item.title: Ancep raises $8.5 million
item.description: London-based insurance startup Ancep has raised $8.5 million in a funding round led by Creandum, with participation from Kleiner Perkins, Vicus Ventures, and angel investors including Christa Davies, former CFO of Aon, and operators from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind. ancep is using AI to change that equation while keeping brokers at the center. We’re excited to support Gagan, Jake, and the ancep team as they expand what brokers can profitably serve.” – Mamoon Hamid, Partner at Kleiner Perkins.

item.title: SelectQuote narrows loss as revenue falls 15%
item.description: SelectQuote Insurance Services reported revenue of $280 million for its fiscal first quarter ended September 30, 2026. Senior revenue declined 14% to $50.8 million, while the segment’s adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $12.3 million from $21 million. SelectQuote maintained its fiscal 2027 outlook: revenue of $1.35 billion to $1.45 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $90 million to $115 million, and operating cash flow above $60 million.

item.title: WSIB Cuts Employer Registration from Days to Minutes With Guidewire
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) Ontario’s Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB, Toronto) has modernized its employer-registration process using Guidewire (San Mateo, Calif.) Jutro Digital Platform, reducing a process that previously took eight to 10 business days to under 10 minutes for most applicants. “We wanted the employer registration process to be simple and intuitive while freeing our teams to focus on the complex cases that require human judgment,” comments Greg Morreale, VP, Enterprise Technology Solutions, WSIB. WSIB and Guidewire position the registration project as the digital foundation for future AI capabilities rather than an AI deployment in itself.

item.title: Payment Friction Is a Persistency Issue for Life Insurers
item.description: When payment friction contributes to preventable lapses, carriers lose premium revenue, policyholder lifetime value and future growth opportunities. When payment processes create unnecessary friction, distribution organizations spend time managing administrative issues instead of strengthening customer relationships and generating new business. How often do payment problems create friction between advisors and clients?

item.title: France Says Iran’s Revolutionary Guards Carried Out Fridge Hacks
item.description: “The responsibility for this attack lies with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps,” French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said on Monday in Paris, in a rare direct attribution of the hacks to a foreign power. France has openly pointed the finger at Iran for recent cyberattacks that crippled fridges and created havoc in hundreds of supermarkets across the nation. Related: US Warns of ‘Ongoing Cyber Threat’ to Industrial Refrigeration Systems Barrot, who was speaking on the sidelines of an informal G7 ministerial meeting, said he would be seeking retaliatory measures against Iran and has summoned the country’s ambassador about the matter.

item.title: Cheche partners with CAR Inc on insurance and mobility services
item.description: They also intend to jointly develop products combining insurance coverage with mobility services and connect their distribution networks across online and physical channels. Cheche provides embedded insurance software, AI-based pricing and digital claims services. Chinese auto insurance technology company Cheche Group is partnering with car rental provider CAR Inc.

item.title: Manulife John Hancock plans private markets retirement funds
item.description: Manulife John Hancock Retirement is partnering with Great Gray Trust Company to develop Lifetime Blend+, a proposed suite of target-date collective investment trusts that would give defined contribution retirement plan participants exposure to private markets. As of September 30, 2026, Manulife John Hancock Retirement serviced more than 56,000 retirement plans covering over 3.3 million participants, with more than $278 billion in assets under management and administration. The funds would be available only through eligible retirement plans, with private-market exposure carrying risks including limited liquidity, valuation complexity and higher fees.

item.title: Acceptiv brings Amore life insurance quotes to ChatGPT
item.description: Canadian insurance technology company Acceptiv has introduced Amore Insurance Quick Quote, a ChatGPT app that provides term life insurance quotes for eligible Canadian applicants. Acceptiv, founded in 2014 by Kevin Pledge, develops RiskDX, a digital life insurance distribution platform covering quotes, applications, automated underwriting, electronic signatures and policy delivery. The app checks available coverage amounts and policy terms, calculates premiums and creates shareable quotes.

item.title: Reale acerca su estrategia para el Canal de Corredores
item.description: Reale Seguros ha organizado el Congreso Titanium 2026, que congregó en el Auditorio Reale a cerca de 100 asistentes entre corredores y empleados.
